idiom_name: one mapper object, class or function set per pair of representations, invoked by the boundary (service layer, gateway, endpoint, ORM or serializer hook)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep both representations ignorant of each other, declare one mapper per pair, and give every translation rule a home there - field names, structure, types, units, defaults, absent-versus-null and what is deliberately dropped. Write the two directions as separate named operations (to_target / from_source) because their policies usually differ, and keep them pure: no queries, no I/O, no business rules. The mapper must be invoked by a third party - a service layer, gateway, endpoint, interceptor or framework hook - since neither representation should call it directly; choose that trigger deliberately and keep it the only one. Where a conversion recurs mechanically across many shapes, move that part to a declarative or generated mapping (annotations, profiles, attributes, schema) and keep hand-written mappers for the conversions that carry real semantics. Protect against drift with tests or generation: adding a field on one side must fail something.
pitfalls: Letting either side hold a reference to the other side's type re-couples the subsystems and undoes the pattern.
Mapping that renames members but ignores semantics (units, time zones, absent versus default, unknown enum values) produces plausible wrong data.
A mapper that grows validation or business rules becomes a shadow domain model nobody owns.
No policy for unknown and newly added fields: one direction drops them silently and the other invents defaults.
